stem: An analytics role in account B needs to read objects in an S3 bucket that account A owns. The role's identity-based policy in account B already allows s3:GetObject on the bucket's objects, but requests are still denied. Without sharing any long-term credentials, what should the data team in account A add?

choices.text: An SCP in account A's organization that allows the account B role to call s3:GetObject on the bucket
Use AWS DataSync to copy the bucket's objects into a bucket in account B
Add a bucket ACL that grants read access to account B's AWS account
A bucket policy that allows s3:GetObject on the bucket's objects for the account B role's ARN

rationale: For a request from one account to another, the requester needs an identity-based policy in its own account and the resource-based policy in the owning account must also allow it. The role already has the first half, so account A adds a bucket policy that names the role and allows s3:GetObject. An SCP never grants permissions; it only limits the maximum permissions of principals in member accounts. AWS DataSync copies data between locations; it does not grant the account B role permission to read the original bucket in account A, and the analytics role's identity-based policy already targets that original object, not a copy sitting in a different bucket. A bucket ACL, even where still enabled, grants access to the whole AWS account rather than to the specific role's ARN, and new S3 buckets default to the Bucket owner enforced setting, which disables ACLs entirely; a bucket policy is the supported way to scope resource-based access to one caller's ARN.
